scope: Production copy retains returned whole-work outcomes through explicit worker context cleanup; grouped pre-return partial effects remain outside this scope
contracts: Effectful resources live in an explicit context; a function pointer has no owned cleanup captures
Supervisor-owned storage receives the returned result before context destruction; completion awaits worker termination
Work and context cleanup have separate unwind boundaries; one panic in each phase does not double-unwind abort
Success retains its exact value plus bounded cleanup warning; ordinary error survives clean cleanup; failed work plus failed cleanup is uncertain with both diagnostics
Production copy preserves exact native replacement history action and ordinary-copy cleanup warnings
Aborting the async waiter does not shorten already-running blocking context lifetime; existing native run_forward owns production continuation

repro.failure: Confirmed result erased by context destructor panic before publication; regression fails on loss-prone ordering and passes in final Rust run

rust.command: cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --offline --lib -- diagnostics:: files::worker:: files::recovery:: renderer_owner:: file_mutation:: file_history:: git_watch:: files::fs_watcher:: task_registry:: files::file_ops:: files::batch:: --test-threads=1

native.build_command: VITE_E2E_HOOKS=1 bun run tauri build --debug --no-bundle --features e2e-renderer-recovery
native.scope: Production singleton overwrite Undo/Redo, recovery, renderer reload and destruction, detached inverse settlement. Cleanup-fault retention is Rust test evidence, not native injected-fault evidence. Checksums bracket one run.

bundle.scope: Ordinary production frontend restored; no startup timing or throughput measurement

independent_review.evidence: Current source, Rust/Clippy/native logs and diff reviewed independently; no unresolved blocker in this scope

limitations: A panic before returning the whole-work result still needs per-item receipts outside the complete worker
Multiple context destructors panicking during cleanup unwinding can still abort; production CopyWork has no such custom destructors
No mixed ordinary/replacement native transfer command, grouped forward-history settlement, paste/drop batch IPC, or one batch progress/cancellation owner yet
Ordinary-copy history remains path-based; exact published-object inverse identity is required before safe native grouping
Other mutation families, artifact retirement and quotas, cross-filesystem and Windows/macOS acceptance, long soaks and final integration remain open
No Mac half-bounce measurement, full-review completion, commit, push or merge is claimed
